qualitative.gate_2_reason: Discretionary leisure destination and casino gaming deferrable in recessions; societal and regulatory acceptance risk from addictive gambling models.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (Rejected – G2 Essential Need). VICI is an experiential and gaming REIT whose revenues derive overwhelmingly (74% tenant concentration across Caesars and MGM) from casino gaming, destination hospitality, and entertainment resorts. Destination casino gambling is a discretionary, episodic leisure expense easily deferred in economic downturns, failing Munger's 'likely to spend' standard, while carrying inherent societal and regulatory acceptance risk as an addictive vice industry.
qualitative.evidence: VICI Properties Inc. owns 93 experiential assets including iconic Las Vegas Strip properties (Caesars Palace, MGM Grand, The Venetian) and regional casinos, operating under long-term triple-net master leases. While leases have 30+ year terms with CPI escalators, tenant concentration is extreme: Caesars Entertainment (~$1.3B) and MGM Resorts (~$1.1B) accounted for ~74% of FY2024 ($3.85B) and FY2025 ($4.01B) total revenues. Underlying tenant cash flows depend on discretionary consumer gaming volumes and resort travel. Furthermore, 10-year median ROIC of 7.2% reflects capital-intensive real estate asset accumulation, and total debt of ~$17.1B represents a high 6.1x multiple against FY2025 net income of $2.80B (net debt/EBITDA ~4.4x–5.0x), precluding compounder status.
